samples.summary: CLI login now hard-requires the backend to echo `state`, breaking every `wafflebase login` against any server older than this change (deploy/publish ordering)
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:280 refuses any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, and the backend only appends `&state=` when it stored a nonce (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:131-135 — added in this same diff). The CLI is a separately versioned npm artifact (`packages/cli/package.json` `bin`, version 0.6.4) while the backend is deployed independently, so a user who upgrades the CLI before the server upgrade gets a 30s hang and a hard failure on the only login path. The reverse (old CLI, new backend) is fine. There is no version negotiation or fallback — only the diagnostic text in REFUSAL.noState. Fix belongs on the new CLI code (e.g. accept a missing `state` from a server that also did not accept a nonce, or gate on a server capability/version).

samples.summary: Hunter charter invariant "the same data under --format json and --format csv agrees" is invalidated by CSV formula neutralization
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/charters/round-trip.md:19 instructs the agent hunter to assert that JSON and CSV renderings of the same data agree. With packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:61 now passing `neutralizeFormulas: true`, a cell whose `formula` is `=SUM(B2:B100)` renders as `'=SUM(B2:B100)` under `--format csv` but unchanged under `--format json`, so the charter will now produce a false-positive defect report. The charter file was not updated with the rest of the docs.

samples.summary: Public developer docs still document the old `--format csv` contract; the new `'` neutralization prefix is undocumented outside docs/design
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:622-627 shows sample `--format csv` output for `sheets cells get` with no mention that values starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR are now emitted with a leading `'`. docs/design/cli.md:866-883 was updated, but the user-facing documentation package (which also documents `--format csv` as a data path for piping) was not, so consumers piping `--format csv` output into other tools get silently altered values.

samples.summary: `ctx list` changed from exit 0 + prose to exit 1 + NOT_LOGGED_IN when logged out; any script/`set -e` wrapper that probed it now aborts
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:78 throws NotLoggedInError (exit 1 via outputError) where the previous implementation printed prose and returned 0. I could not find an in-repo consumer (scripts/agent/hunt-workspace.mjs resolves from config sources instead), so the blast radius is limited to out-of-repo scripts and agent skills that shell out to `ctx list` as a liveness probe. Flagging because the exit-code contract of a read-only command changed without a compatibility note in packages/cli/README.md.

finding.summary: CLI login now hard-requires the backend to echo `state`, breaking every `wafflebase login` against any server older than this change (deploy/publish ordering)
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:280 refuses any callback whose `state` does not match the nonce, and the backend only appends `&state=` when it stored a nonce (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:131-135 — added in this same diff). The CLI is a separately versioned npm artifact (`packages/cli/package.json` `bin`, version 0.6.4) while the backend is deployed independently, so a user who upgrades the CLI before the server upgrade gets a 30s hang and a hard failure on the only login path. The reverse (old CLI, new backend) is fine. There is no version negotiation or fallback — only the diagnostic text in REFUSAL.noState. Fix belongs on the new CLI code (e.g. accept a missing `state` from a server that also did not accept a nonce, or gate on a server capability/version).

verdict.reason: The code exists as described (login.ts:280 refuses non-matching state; auth.controller.ts:131-136 appends state only when a nonce was stored), but it is not a blast-radius defect. Every in-repo consumer of the contract is updated and consistent: the nonce is parsed/stored in github-auth.guard.ts:36-40 and cli-auth.store.ts:27-62, echoed in auth.controller.ts:131-136, and documented in docs/design/rest-api.md:334,347. A repo-wide grep for startCallbackServer/nonceMatches/mode=cli//callback?code= finds no other reference relying on the old (state-less) behaviour; the `state.nonce ?` conditional is itself the old-CLI/new-backend compatibility shim. Nothing bypasses the new guard — the finding asks for the guard to be relaxed for older deployed servers, and the only suggested remedy (accept a missing `state`) reopens the login-CSRF vector the guard closes, which is the security lens's territory, not this one. The claimed impact is also softer than stated: the refusal is printed immediately (login.ts:240-249) and named in the timeout error (login.ts:206-209), with that exact old-server case covered by packages/cli/test/login.test.ts:101-121. What remains is a release/deploy-ordering and docs concern with no broken call site in this repository.

finding.summary: `sheets export --file-format csv` inherits the new CSV formula neutralization and corrupts exported data
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46 calls the shared `formatCsv(res.data)` directly (not through `output()`), so the new `neutralizeFormula` in packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts now prefixes every exported formula/value starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR with `'`. That path is a file/stdout export of sheet content, not a human-facing render: the documented pipeline `wafflebase sheets export "$DOC_ID" out.csv` (packages/cli/skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md:44, docs/design/cli.md:1064) exports cells that contain `=SUM(B2:B100)` and re-imports them via `sheets import` (parseCsv → buildCellMap), which will now write the literal text `'=SUM(B2:B100)`. The design doc scopes the neutralization to the `--format csv` render path only (docs/design/cli.md:854-858) and says nothing about `--file-format csv` export, so this consumer was not considered. Fix belongs on the new code: keep neutralization in the `output()`/`format()` path (or make it opt-in) rather than inside `formatCsv` itself.

verdict.reason: The claimed bypassing site does not exist as described. `formatCsv` does not apply neutralization unconditionally: packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:40-58 declares a required (non-defaulted) `CsvOptions.neutralizeFormulas: boolean`, and csv.ts:74 gates the call — `const s = options.neutralizeFormulas ? neutralizeFormula(raw) : raw;`. The export command does NOT call `formatCsv(res.data)`; packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:52 calls `formatCsv(res.data, { neutralizeFormulas: false })`, with an in-code comment at lines 47-49 naming the `sheets import` round-trip as the reason. Because the option is required, a no-argument call would not even type-check. A repo-wide grep for `formatCsv` finds only two production call sites: packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:61 (render path, `true`) and sheets-export.ts:52 (interchange path, `false`); all other hits are tests (packages/cli/test/output.test.ts) or docs. So an exported `=SUM(B2:B100)` is written verbatim and re-imports as a formula — no data corruption. The fix the finding prescribes ("keep neutralization in the output()/format() path rather than inside formatCsv") is precisely what is already implemented and documented at docs/design/cli.md:875-883. No broken caller, no over-applied contract, nothing for the blast-radius lens to block on.
